title: VM provisioning and ./lab VM lifecycle
objective: Make the VM reproducible and controllable from the host: ./lab can provision or connect to the VM per #40, install Docker, transport the workspace, and run VM lifecycle commands idempotently. The host stops running the agent container itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: One documented command/runbook takes a clean host to a working VM (Docker plus compose plugin, repo checkout, agent image) with a CPU-only path that works without a GPU.
./lab gains VM lifecycle commands (names fixed by #40, for example vm up/status/ssh/down) that are idempotent: re-running does not duplicate VMs, disks or networks.

check_workspace() validation still runs on the host before a path is sent to the VM; /, $HOME, the lab repo without --unsafe-recurse, and sensitive credential directories are refused and never mounted.
The VM publishes no host ports by default; an automated check confirms the agent and workspace services are reachable only on the VM's internal Docker networks.

Model access follows #40: host-side ollama/llamacpp are reachable only through the narrow guestfwd ports; GPU passthrough is not required, and a CPU-only host starts with the same flow and a clear message.
./lab stop removes agent containers plus workspace containers, networks and volumes and VM-side state; git status --short in the real checkout is empty afterwards.
./verify-lab.sh passes from a clean clone inside the VM, and the run is recorded on this ticket.

The host no longer runs the agent container; any host-side Docker use is limited to a documented service (for example model servers) if #40 chooses that option. README and docs/01-host-setup.md describe the VM flow and remove dev-container-only instructions.
